stages.title: A real token
stages.desc: The Flutter app signs in with Firebase and gets an ID token.
stages.narration: The Flutter app signs in and sends its Firebase token.

stages.title: Issuer and audience
stages.desc: Issuer securetoken.google.com/PROJECT_ID, audience the project ID.
stages.narration: Validate the issuer, the audience, and the signature. Exactly.

stages.title: The 401 that names nothing
stages.desc: A bare 401 hides the real mismatch. The exception message names it.
stages.status: expected audience vs the one that arrived
stages.narration: When it fails, read the exception. The bare four oh one names nothing.

stages.title: Roles from claims
stages.desc: Set with the Admin SDK. Never from a field the client sends.
stages.narration: Roles come from custom claims set server side. Never from the client.

stages.title: No secret to leak
stages.desc: App Service gets a system-assigned managed identity.
stages.narration: Deploy to App Service with a managed identity. No key exists.

stages.title: Foundry User, for the app
stages.desc: The identity gets the Foundry User role on the project.
stages.status: role assignment on the Foundry project
stages.narration: Give that identity the Foundry User role on the project.

stages.title: SQL without a password
stages.desc: CREATE USER FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER. The local password stays local.
stages.narration: Even SQL Server opens with the same identity. No password in production.

stages.title: Smoke test
stages.desc: 200 with a token, 401 without, and an answer from the agent.
stages.narration: Smoke test after deploy: two hundred with a token, four oh one without.

stages.title: Token in, no secret anywhere
stages.desc: Roles from custom claims, and a managed identity for Foundry and SQL.

end.title: Token in. No secret anywhere.
end.sub: Roles from custom claims, then a managed identity so no key exists to leak.

post.caption:
Firebase token in. No secret anywhere. 🪪

Validating a Firebase ID token in ASP.NET Core: issuer https://securetoken.google.com/PROJECT_ID, audience the project ID itself.

Roles come from custom claims set with the Admin SDK, never from a field the client sends.

Deploy to App Service with a system-assigned managed identity. Give it Foundry User on the project and a SQL user from EXTERNAL PROVIDER. No key, no password, nothing to leak.

Full article: blog.msdevbuild.com/blog/firebase-auth-aspnet-core-azure-deploy-managed-identity
